boundary_evidence: One contiguous run of the Nitro SDK's spi tp.c, 0x0205e9fc..0x0205f5c0: 14 functions, gapless in config/arm9/delinks.txt. Each is identified by its body against ntrtwl/NitroSDK libraries/spi/src/tp.c. TPi_TpCallback is the PXI tag 6 receive callback TP_Init installs: it splits the reply word into command ((result & 0x7f00) >> 8) and result, copies the panel sample from the system work area (0x027fffaa) for SPI_PXI_COMMAND_TP_SAMPLING and AUTO_SAMPLING (0x10), sets tpState.state, err_flg and command_flg, maps the SPI results 2/3/4 to TP_RESULT_INVALID_PARAMETER/ILLEGAL_STATUS/EXCLUSIVE (1/2/3) and an error to TP_RESULT_PXI_BUSY (4) for the user callback, and stops on any other result. TP_SetCalibrateParam computes each axis's inverse dot size with the CP divider (0x10000000 / dot size). TP_CalcCalibrateParam, TP_GetCalibratedPoint, the request senders (commands 0, 1 and 3 with START_BIT 0x02000000 / END_BIT 0x01000000), TP_WaitBusy and TP_CheckError follow the SDK step for step.

Order: mwccarm emits the bodies in reverse. The SDK's file order of the surviving functions is TPi_TpCallback, TP_Init, TP_GetUserInfo, TP_SetCalibrateParam, TP_RequestSamplingAsync, TP_GetCalibratedResult, TP_WaitCalibratedResult, TP_RequestAutoSamplingStartAsync, TP_RequestSetStabilityAsync, TP_GetLatestIndexInAuto, TP_CalcCalibrateParam, TP_GetCalibratedPoint, TP_WaitBusy, TP_CheckError, and the ROM holds exactly that reversed. The SDK functions nothing calls (TP_SetCallback, TP_WaitRawResult, TP_RequestAutoSamplingStopAsync, TP_GetLatestRawPointInAuto, TP_GetLatestCalibratedPointInAuto, TP_GetUnCalibratedPoint, TP_WaitAllBusy, TP_CheckBusy) are dead-stripped.
BOTTOM EDGE: the DGT functions below 0x0205e9fc reference data_020a80c4, not tp.c's state.
TOP EDGE: PMi_SendLEDPatternCommand at 0x0205f5c0, the lowest function of pm.c (arm9/PM).

.bss: TP_Init's function-local `static u16 initial` (0x020a80c8, 2 bytes, padded to 4) and the file-scope tpState (0x020a80cc, 0x38 bytes). Only TP_Init references initial (0x0205f2f4); every function references tpState, and TP_GetCalibratedPoint's literal pool names &tpState.calibrate (0x020a80e4). Above, PMi_IsInit (0x020a8104) starts pm.c's .bss; below, data_020a80c4 is the DGT code's (0x0205e6dc, 0x0205e918).

bss.evidence: TP_Init's function-local `static u16 initial = FALSE`, the SDK's once-only guard: TP_Init tests it and sets it to TRUE before PXI_Init. Its only reference is TP_Init's (0x0205f2f4, config/arm9/relocs.txt).

The SDK's file-scope `static struct { ... } tpState`: callback, buf, index, frequence, samplingBufs, bufSize, calibrate (TPiCalibrateParam, +0x18), calibrate_flg, and the volatile state / err_flg / command_flg halfwords at +0x32..+0x36. 0x38 bytes, ending where pm.c's PMi_IsInit begins (0x020a8104). Only tp.c's functions reference it.

symbol_binding_rewrites.evidence: function-local static, as the SDK writes it; DSD requires a configured global symbol at 0x020a80c8, and changing the ELF binding preserves its function-local lifetime, storage, relocations and bytes
file-scope static, as the SDK writes it; dsd cannot record a local symbol in symbols.txt, so the owned object is published global at 0x020a80cc
static in the SDK; TP_Init passes its address to PXI_SetFifoRecvCallback (0x0205f2fc), so it is published global at 0x0205f300 for symbols.txt

notes: HAND-BUILT manifest entry, not tools/tubuild.py create output: tu_map does not segment arm9.
Built as C. The API and its types are the SDK's nitro/spi/ARM9/tp.h, in include/nitro/spi/tp.h; tpState and TPiCalibrateParam are tp.c's own and stay in the source.

The .bss names come from the SDK source: data_020a80c8 is TP_Init's initial (its compiler spelling, initial$180, as d_camera.cpp's function-local statics are named) and data_020a80cc is tpState. data_020a80e4 keeps its address name: it is &tpState.calibrate, which TP_GetCalibratedPoint's literal pool names, and dsd needs a symbol at every relocation target.

This SDK is older than the ntrtwl/NitroSDK copy: TP_RequestSetStabilityAsync sends the retry count and the range as two words (the later SDK sends the range alone), TP_SetCalibrateParam has no zero-dot-size branch, and TP_GetUserInfo returns FALSE when the calibration is absent or rejected instead of clearing it and returning TRUE.
